role: Clipboard and incoming shared-text lifecycle, duplicate delivery, and main-thread parsing

scope.application_commit_reviewed: e625ee7 with unrelated network/runtime changes in progress; parent handling reviewer52 share-intent construction separately
scope.method: Read-only static control-flow, algorithmic-complexity and existing test-source review. No build, runtime test, device action, production edit or publication.

findings.title: Pasted or shared trailing delimiters cause quadratic parsing on the UI thread
findings.evidence: shared(text) permits up to 32768 input characters. For each removed unmatched trailing closing delimiter, its while condition counts the full candidate twice and dropLast copies another large string. Both MainActivity.receive -> MainViewModel.receive and the Paste UI -> MainViewModel.paste -> receive call Safety.shared synchronously. The candidate URL length limit of8192 is checked only by url(candidate), after stripping.
findings.trigger_and_impact: A single input consisting of https://example.com/a followed by 32000 right parentheses remains under the shared-text length cap. It causes approximately quadratic character scanning/copying before returning the short URL, unnecessarily blocking the UI and allocating many transient strings. No actual ANR or elapsed-time threshold was measured.
findings.recommendation: Calculate opening/closing delimiter counts once per pair; move an end index backward while decrementing the excess closing count, and create the resulting substring once. Preserve balanced literal parentheses/brackets and existing Arabic prose delimiter behavior. Add a long-suffix functional regression and verify complexity without a fragile device-speed assertion.
findings.status: Reported to parent; this reviewer made no edits.

verified_observations: The clipboard UI reads ClipData.Item.text and does not call coerceToText; image/URI-only clips therefore do not trigger content-provider text reads. Existing test source expects Nothing to paste for null, ordinary text and content-only clipboard input.

MainActivity accepts CharSequence EXTRA_TEXT, removes that extra after delivery, and handles new deliveries through onNewIntent. Ordinary state recreation restores draft/pending text instead of re-delivering the launch extra.

Busy analysis, batch restoration, batch saving and draft-error states defer incoming text in pendingShared. acceptPending rechecks those gates before consuming it; the existing failed-draft recovery test verifies deferred acceptance in its source.
Multiple HTTP links route to batch review without immediately analyzing every link. Canonicalized duplicate batch URLs are filtered.

Analysis marks its busy state before launch; source ownership and cancellation guardians prevent an overlapping input from directly replacing an active extraction. This observation is static, with no latency measurement.
limitations: No clipboard service, incoming Intent or process-death delivery was exercised during this audit.
The latest pendingShared slot retains a single incoming text; multi-message inbox behavior was not invented as a requirement.
The algorithmic issue is established from the loops and input bounds. Its exact user-visible duration and whether a particular device reaches an ANR are unmeasured.
Reviewer52's already-reported outgoing-share provider-query issue was excluded from this independent finding count.
